namespace igl {
/**
 * @brief Helper class simplifying the creation of IShaderLibrary instances in common scenarios.
 */
class ShaderLibraryCreator {
 public:
  ShaderLibraryCreator() = delete;
  /**
   * @brief Constructs an IShaderLibrary with a vertex and fragment shader from source code.
   * @param device The device to construct the shader library with.
   * @param librarySource Null-terminated string containing shader source code.
   * @param vertexEntryPoint Vertex shader entry point name.
   * @param fragmentEntryPoint Fragment shader entry point name.
   * @param libraryDebugName Optional debug name for the library.
   * @param outResult Optional param to receive success or error information.
   */
  static std::unique_ptr<IShaderLibrary> fromStringInput(const IDevice& device,
                                                         const char* IGL_NONNULL librarySource,
                                                         std::string vertexEntryPoint,
                                                         std::string fragmentEntryPoint,
                                                         std::string libraryDebugName,
                                                         Result* IGL_NULLABLE outResult);
  /**
   * @brief Constructs an IShaderLibrary with a vertex and fragment shader from binary data.
   * @param device The device to construct the shader library with.
   * @param libraryData Pre-compiled shader binary data.
   * @param libraryDataLength Length in bytes of the precompiled shader binary data.
   * @param vertexEntryPoint Vertex shader entry point name.
   * @param fragmentEntryPoint Fragment shader entry point name.
   * @param libraryDebugName Optional debug name for the library.
   * @param outResult Optional param to receive success or error information.
   */
  static std::unique_ptr<IShaderLibrary> fromBinaryInput(const IDevice& device,
                                                         const void* IGL_NONNULL libraryData,
                                                         size_t libraryDataLength,
                                                         std::string vertexEntryPoint,
                                                         std::string fragmentEntryPoint,
                                                         std::string libraryDebugName,
                                                         Result* IGL_NULLABLE outResult);

  /**
   * @brief Constructs an IShaderLibrary with shaders from source code.
   * @param device The device to construct the shader library with.
   * @param librarySource Null-terminated string containing shader source code.
   * @param moduleInfo Vector of metadata for shader modules in the library.
   * @param libraryDebugName Optional debug name for the library.
   * @param outResult Optional param to receive success or error information.
   */
  static std::unique_ptr<IShaderLibrary> fromStringInput(const IDevice& device,
                                                         const char* IGL_NONNULL librarySource,
                                                         std::vector<ShaderModuleInfo> moduleInfo,
                                                         std::string libraryDebugName,
                                                         Result* IGL_NULLABLE outResult);

  /**
   * @brief Constructs an IShaderLibrary with shaders from binary data.
   * @param device The device to construct the shader library with.
   * @param libraryData Pre-compiled shader binary data.
   * @param libraryDataLength Length in bytes of the precompiled shader binary data.
   * @param moduleInfo Vector of metadata for shader modules in the library.
   * @param libraryDebugName Optional debug name for the library.
   * @param outResult Optional param to receive success or error information.
   */
  static std::unique_ptr<IShaderLibrary> fromBinaryInput(const IDevice& device,
                                                         const void* IGL_NONNULL libraryData,
                                                         size_t libraryDataLength,
                                                         std::vector<ShaderModuleInfo> moduleInfo,
                                                         std::string libraryDebugName,
                                                         Result* IGL_NULLABLE outResult);
};
objects.description: A non-instantiable helper class with static factories to build IShaderLibrary instances from source or binary inputs, either for a fixed vertex/fragment pair or for a set of modules described by ShaderModuleInfo.

                                                              std::string fragmentEntryPoint,

                                                              const void* IGL_NONNULL fragmentData,

   * @param vertexEntryPoint Vertex shader entry point name.

   * @param outResult Optional param to receive success or error information.

                                                               std::string vertexEntryPoint,
                                                               std::string fragmentEntryPoint,
                                                               std::string libraryDebugName,
                                                               Result* IGL_NULLABLE outResult);

  /**
   * @brief Constructs IShaderStages for a compute shader from module source code.

functions.name: try_checked_memcpy
functions.signature: int try_checked_memcpy(void* destination, size_t destination_size, const void* source, size_t count)
functions.description: Copies count bytes from source to destination if destination has at least destination_size bytes and destination_size >= count. On insufficient destination capacity, returns an error code instead of copying. Intended as a safer memcpy-like helper that reports overflow risk via return value.
requirements: destination must point to a buffer of at least destination_size bytes.
destination_size must be >= count; otherwise no copy occurs and ERR_POTENTIAL_BUFFER_OVERFLOW (34) is returned.
source must point to at least count readable bytes; this function cannot validate source size.
The source and destination regions must not overlap (memcpy requirement).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates no copy performed due to potential overflow.
Passing NULL for destination or source is only valid if count == 0 (memcpy rule); otherwise behavior is undefined.

functions.name: checked_memcpy
functions.signature: void* checked_memcpy(void* destination, size_t destination_size, const void* source, size_t count)
functions.description: Copies count bytes from source to destination after verifying destination_size >= count. If the size check fails, the function reports a verification failure and terminates the process via exit(EXIT_FAILURE). Mirrors memcpy semantics on success and returns destination.
requirements: destination must point to a buffer of at least destination_size bytes.
destination_size must be >= count; otherwise the process terminates.
source must point to at least count readable bytes; this function does not verify source size.
The source and destination regions must not overlap (memcpy requirement).
On success, the return value equals destination.
Passing NULL for destination or source is only valid if count == 0 (memcpy rule).

functions.name: checked_memcpy_robust
functions.signature: void* checked_memcpy_robust(void* destination, size_t destination_size, const void* source, size_t source_size, size_t count)
functions.description: Copies count bytes from source to destination after verifying both destination_size >= count and source_size >= count. If either check fails, it reports a verification failure and terminates the process via exit(EXIT_FAILURE). Mirrors memcpy semantics on success and returns destination.
requirements: destination must point to a buffer of at least destination_size bytes.
source must point to a buffer of at least source_size bytes.
destination_size must be >= count and source_size must be >= count; otherwise the process terminates.
The source and destination regions must not overlap (memcpy requirement).
On success, the return value equals destination.
Passing NULL for destination or source is only valid if count == 0 (memcpy rule).

functions.name: checked_memcpy_offset
functions.signature: void* checked_memcpy_offset(void* destination, size_t destination_size, size_t offset, const void* source, size_t count)
functions.description: Copies count bytes from source into destination starting at byte offset within destination. It computes available_size = destination_size - offset (clamped at 0) and verifies count <= available_size to prevent overflow; otherwise it reports a verification failure and terminates the process via exit(EXIT_FAILURE). Returns destination on success.
requirements: destination must point to a buffer of at least destination_size bytes.

offset must be such that offset <= destination_size; effective available_size is destination_size - offset (if offset > destination_size, available_size is treated as 0 and the function will terminate if count > 0).
count must be <= destination_size - offset; otherwise the process terminates.
source must point to at least count readable bytes.
The source and destination regions (destination+offset .. +offset+count) must not overlap with source (memcpy requirement).
On success, the return value equals destination.
Passing NULL for destination or source is only valid if count == 0 and offset is within range (memcpy rule).

functions.name: checked_strncmp
functions.signature: int checked_strncmp(const char* str1, size_t str1_size, const char* str2, size_t str2_size, size_t count)
functions.description: Compares up to count characters of str1 and str2 using strncmp after verifying str1_size >= count and str2_size >= count to avoid overreads. If either size check fails, it reports a verification failure and terminates the process via exit(EXIT_FAILURE). Returns the same tri-state result as strncmp on success.
requirements: str1 must point to a buffer of at least str1_size bytes; str2 must point to a buffer of at least str2_size bytes.
str1_size must be >= count and str2_size must be >= count; otherwise the process terminates.
Buffers need not be null-terminated; comparison is limited to count bytes like strncmp.
Passing NULL for str1 or str2 is only valid if count == 0 (strncmp/memcmp rule).
Caller should interpret the return value as in strncmp: <0 if str1 < str2, 0 if equal up to count, >0 if str1 > str2.

functions.description: Destructor for a tracked resource base. If a tracker was previously set via initResourceTracker(), the resource notifies the tracker that it is about to be deleted (willDelete). Intended for CRTP-style inheritance (derived classes inherit as ITrackedResource<Derived>). Normally not called directly by users; invoked when the resource object is destroyed.
requirements: No explicit caller requirements; this destructor is invoked automatically when the object is destroyed.
If a tracker was set, it must be capable of handling willDelete(T*) during object teardown.
Class must be used with the correct CRTP pattern: the derived type should inherit as ITrackedResource<DerivedType> so that static_cast<T*>(this) is valid.

functions.name: igl::ITrackedResource::initResourceTracker
functions.signature:
template <class T>
void igl::ITrackedResource<T>::initResourceTracker(std::shared_ptr<igl::IResourceTracker> tracker, const std::string& name = "")
functions.description: Registers this resource instance with a resource tracker and assigns an optional human-readable name. On success, the tracker is stored and didCreate(this) is called. When the resource is later destroyed, the tracker will be notified via willDelete(this). Call this during resource initialization to enable tracking. Passing a null tracker is allowed; in that case no registration occurs but the name is still stored.
requirements: Must be called at most once per resource instance; calling when a tracker is already set is disallowed in debug builds (guarded by IGL_DEBUG_VERIFY) and will be a no-op.
Should be called during/after successful initialization of the resource so that didCreate(this) observes a valid object state.
tracker may be null; if null, no didCreate() is invoked and no destruction callback will occur.
name may be empty; it is used for identification only and has no functional effect.
The class must be instantiated with the correct derived type (CRTP): ITrackedResource<DerivedType>, so that passing static_cast<T*>(this) to the tracker is valid.

functions.name: igl::ITrackedResource::getResourceName
functions.signature:
template <class T>
[[nodiscard]] virtual const std::string& igl::ITrackedResource<T>::getResourceName() const
functions.description: Returns the resource's assigned name as a constant reference. If no name was set, this may be an empty string. Marked [[nodiscard]] to encourage callers to use the value.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only for the lifetime of the resource object; do not store or use it after the object is destroyed.
The returned string may be empty if no name was provided to initResourceTracker().

functions.name: IGLLog
functions.signature: IGL_API int IGLLog(IGLLogLevel logLevel, const char* IGL_RESTRICT format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a message at the given IGLLogLevel using a printf-style format string and variadic arguments. Intended for general logging within the IGL library or clients. The exact meaning of the returned int is not documented in this header (likely implementation-defined).
requirements: logLevel must be a valid IGLLogLevel value (IGLLogError, IGLLogWarning, or IGLLogInfo).

Behavior and return value semantics are otherwise unknown from this header.

functions.name: IGLLogOnce

functions.description: Logs a message similarly to IGLLog, but only once. Useful for suppressing duplicate logs. The scope of "once" (per process, per call site, etc.) is not specified in this header. Return value semantics are not documented.
requirements: logLevel must be a valid IGLLogLevel value (IGLLogError, IGLLogWarning, or IGLLogInfo).
format must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
The variadic arguments must match the printf-style specifiers present in format.
The exact conditions that determine "once" are unspecified in this header.

functions.name: IGLLogV
functions.signature: IGL_API int IGLLogV(IGLLogLevel logLevel, const char* IGL_RESTRICT format, va_list arguments);
functions.description: Logs a message at the given level using a printf-style format string and a va_list of arguments. This is the va_list-based variant of IGLLog for callers that already have a variable argument list. Return value semantics are not documented here.
requirements: logLevel must be a valid IGLLogLevel value (IGLLogError, IGLLogWarning, or IGLLogInfo).
format must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
arguments must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to the specifiers in format and valid for use at the time of the call.

functions.name: IGLLogDefaultHandler

functions.description: The library’s built-in log handler. Formats and emits a log message for the given level using the provided printf-style format string and va_list. Typically used internally or as a fallback when no custom handler is set. Exact return value semantics are not documented.
requirements: logLevel must be a valid IGLLogLevel value (IGLLogError, IGLLogWarning, or IGLLogInfo).
format must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
ap must be a valid, initialized va_list that matches the specifiers in format.

functions.name: IGLLogSetHandler
functions.description: Sets the global/custom log handler function used by the logging system. Allows clients to intercept and handle logs. Passing a function pointer of type IGLLogHandlerFunc installs it as the active handler. Behavior for a null handler is not specified in this header.
requirements: handler must be a valid function pointer matching IGLLogHandlerFunc (int (*)(IGLLogLevel, const char*, va_list)).
The handler must remain valid (not destroyed/unloaded) for as long as it may be invoked by the logging system.

functions.name: IGLLogGetHandler
functions.description: Returns the currently installed log handler function pointer. Can be used to query or restore a previous handler. The meaning of a null return (if any) is not specified in this header.

functions.name: igl::iglCrc32ConstExpr

p must be readable up to and including the terminating '\0'.

functions.name: igl::iglCrc32ConstExpr
functions.description: Computes a CRC32 checksum of the bytes contained in the provided std::string_view at compile time when possible. Useful for generating deterministic CRC handles from string data without requiring null termination.

functions.name: igl::iglCrc32
functions.signature: uint32_t igl::iglCrc32(const char* data, size_t length)

requirements: data must point to a readable memory region of at least length bytes.
length specifies the number of bytes to include in the CRC computation.

functions.name: igl::NameHandle::c_str
functions.description: Returns a null-terminated C-string pointer to the stored name within the NameHandle. Useful when interoperating with APIs requiring const char*.
requirements: The NameHandle object must be initialized with a name before use.

functions.name: igl::NameHandle::toString
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the stored std::string name. Use when string operations or ownership outside c_str() are required.
requirements: The NameHandle object must be initialized with a name before use.

functions.name: iglStringlength
functions.description: Lightweight strlen equivalent used when constexpr support is unavailable. Counts characters until the first null terminator.

functions.name: std::hash<igl::NameHandle>::operator()
functions.description: Hash functor for igl::NameHandle. Returns a hash derived from the handle’s 32-bit CRC value, enabling use of NameHandle as a key in unordered containers.

functions.signature: size_t std::hash<std::pair<igl::NameHandle, igl::NameHandle>>::operator()(const std::pair<igl::NameHandle, igl::NameHandle>& key) const
functions.description: Hash functor for pairs of igl::NameHandle. Combines the hashes of the CRC values of the two NameHandles for use in unordered containers.

functions.name: igl::IRenderCommandEncoder::bindBuffer
functions.signature: virtual void bindBuffer(uint32_t index, uint8_t target, IBuffer* buffer, size_t bufferOffset = 0, size_t bufferSize = 0) = 0
functions.description: Binds a buffer to a shader stage and binding index. Backend notes: Vulkan: index is the buffer binding index in the shader. Metal: index is the buffer index in the shader. buffer must point to an IBuffer compatible with the current device/backend.

index selects the vertex buffer binding slot (or vertex-stage buffer index on Metal).
bufferOffset is the byte offset into the buffer where vertex data begins.

functions.description: Binds an index buffer for indexed drawing with the specified index format and starting byte offset.

bufferOffset is the byte offset where index data begins.

functions.signature: virtual void bindBytes(size_t index, uint8_t target, const void* data, size_t length) = 0
functions.description: Creates and binds a temporary buffer with the provided raw bytes to the specified binding index and target stage(s). Useful for small uniform/push data without creating a persistent buffer.
requirements: length specifies the number of bytes to bind starting at data.
index selects the binding index; target selects shader stage(s) (e.g., BindTarget values).
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory for the duration of the call.

functions.name: igl::IRenderCommandEncoder::bindPushConstants
functions.signature: virtual void bindPushConstants(const void* data, size_t length, size_t offset = 0) = 0
functions.description: Binds push-constant data to the current encoder. Push constants are small pieces of data passed directly to shaders with low overhead.
requirements: data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
offset specifies the byte offset into the push constant range.
length and offset must comply with backend push-constant size/offset limitations (backend-defined).

functions.name: igl::IRenderCommandEncoder::bindSamplerState
functions.signature: virtual void bindSamplerState(size_t index, uint8_t target, ISamplerState* samplerState) = 0
functions.description: Binds a sampler state object at the given binding index and shader stage target(s). Controls texture sampling behavior (filtering, addressing).
requirements: index selects the sampler binding slot; target selects shader stage(s).
samplerState must reference a valid ISamplerState compatible with the pipeline/backend.

functions.name: igl::IRenderCommandEncoder::bindTexture

texture must reference a valid ITexture compatible with the pipeline/backend.

functions.name: igl::IRenderCommandEncoder::bindUniform
functions.signature: virtual void bindUniform(const UniformDesc& uniformDesc, const void* data) = 0
functions.description: Binds an individual uniform value. Intended exclusively for cases where uniform blocks are not supported.

requirements: handle must be a valid BindGroupTextureHandle created for the current device/context.

functions.name: igl::IRenderCommandEncoder::drawMeshTasks

requirements: indirectBuffer must contain indexed draw parameter structures in a backend-defined layout.
indirectBufferOffset is the byte offset to the first command structure.
drawCount is the number of draw commands; stride is the byte distance between commands (backend may allow 0 to imply tightly packed).

functions.description: Returns a copy of this range with numLayers replaced by newNumLayers.
requirements: newNumLayers >= 1 (validate() enforces).

functions.name: igl::TextureRangeDesc::atFace

requirements: format must be a valid igl::TextureFormat enumerator.

        # Mix small and large values; include boundaries
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            v = rng.choice([0, 1, 1000, 1001, 0xFFFFFFFF & 0, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF])
        elif choice < 0.6:
            v = rng.randrange(0, 100000)
        else:
            v = rng.getrandbits(32)
        buf += struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    labels = _weighted_labels(rng)

    # Randomly shuffle a subset to vary order while keeping deterministic seed
    rng.shuffle(labels)

    # Limit the number of labels to keep total size under 4 KiB with ints appended
    # Estimate: average ~20 bytes per label + 1 null -> 21; 120 labels ~ 2520 bytes
    # Leave space for ~128 uints (512 bytes) and some headroom.
    max_labels = 140
    labels = labels[:max_labels]

    label_bytes = _pack_cstrings(labels)

    # Append a block of random uints that stubs use for colors/alphas
    uint_count = 128
    uint_bytes = _rand_uint_block(rng, uint_count)

    blob = label_bytes + uint_bytes

    # Ensure final size cap
    return blob[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: identifier string
# This generator creates plausible identifier-like UTF-8 strings tailored for
# shader-related APIs (entry points, uniform names, resource names) used by the
# fuzz stubs. It mixes common shader identifiers, stages, prefixes, indices,
# camelCase/snake_case variants, and occasional namespaces. It keeps length
# reasonable and ensures non-empty ASCII strings. Returned as bytes.

_RESERVED_WORDS = [
    # Common GLSL/HLSL keywords and built-ins to exercise lookups
    "main", "vs_main", "fs_main", "cs_main",
    "u_MVP", "u_Model", "u_View", "u_Proj", "u_Time", "u_FrameIndex",
    "u_RandomSeed", "u_Resolution", "u_Color", "u_LightDir", "u_NormalMatrix",
    "a_Position", "a_Normal", "a_Tangent", "a_TexCoord0", "a_TexCoord1",
    "v_Position", "v_Normal", "v_TexCoord", "v_Color",
    "g_Position", "SV_Position", "POSITION", "TEXCOORD0", "COLOR0",
    # Resource-like names
    "tex0", "texAlbedo", "texNormal", "texMetallicRoughness", "texDepth",
    "sampler0", "samplerLinear", "samplerShadow",
    "buffer0", "uboPerFrame", "uboPerObject", "ssboParticles",
]

_STAGE_TAGS = ["VS", "FS", "CS", "TS", "MS", "PS"]
_PREFIXES = ["u_", "a_", "v_", "g_", "s_", "tex", "buffer", "ubo", "ssbo", "pc_", ""]
_SUFFIXES = ["", "0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "X", "Y", "Z", "XY", "ZW", "RGBA", "XYZ"]
_WORDS = [
    "Position", "Normal", "Tangent", "Bitangent", "TexCoord", "TexCoord0", "TexCoord1",
    "Color", "Albedo", "Roughness", "Metallic", "Occlusion", "Emissive",
    "MVP", "Model", "View", "Proj", "ViewProj", "Time", "Frame", "Resolution",
    "Light", "LightDir", "LightColor", "CameraPos", "Jitter", "Noise",
    "Bones", "Weights", "Indices", "InstanceID", "DrawID",
]

_NS_SEPARATORS = ["::", ".", "_"]

def _stage_tag_candidates() -> List[str]:
    # Build a small set of optional stage tag affixes
    cands: List[str] = [""]
    for s in _STAGE_TAGS:
        cands.append("_" + s)
        cands.append(s)
        cands.append("_Stage" + s)
    return cands

def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random, max_parts: int = 3) -> str:
    # Compose identifier from prefix + words + suffix
    prefix = rng.choice(_PREFIXES)
    parts = []
    # Choose 1..max_parts words
    n = rng.randint(1, max_parts)
    for _ in range(n):
        parts.append(rng.choice(_WORDS))
    base = "".join(parts)
    # camelCase or snake_case variation
    style = rng.choice(["camel", "snake", "upper", "lower"]) if base else "camel"
    if style == "snake":
        # split Camel into snake
        snake = []
        for ch in base:
            if ch.isupper() and snake:
                snake.append("_")
            snake.append(ch.lower())
        base = "".join(snake)
    elif style == "upper":
        base = base.upper()
    elif style == "lower":
        base = base.lower()
    # Optional stage tag infix/suffix
    stage = rng.choice(_stage_tag_candidates())
    suffix = rng.choice(_SUFFIXES)
    ident = f"{prefix}{base}{stage}{suffix}"
    # Occasionally add numeric index
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ident += str(rng.randint(0, 15)) if not ident[-1:].isdigit() else ""
    # Ensure first char valid for typical identifiers
    if not ident or not (ident[0].isalpha() or ident[0] == "_"):
        ident = ("_" + ident) if ident else "_id"
    return ident

def _maybe_namespace(rng: random.Random, name: str) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        ns = rng.choice(["igl", "app", "material", "lighting", "postfx"])  # plausible namespaces
        sep = rng.choice(_NS_SEPARATORS)
        return f"{ns}{sep}{name}"
    return name

def _mix_reserved(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice_pool = _RESERVED_WORDS + [
        "mainVS", "mainFS", "mainCS", "entryVS", "entryFS", "entryCS",
        "ComputeMain", "MeshMain", "TaskMain",
    ]
    return rng.choice(choice_pool)

def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(L))
    if not (s[0].isalpha() or s[0] == '_'):
        s = '_' + s
    return s

def _build_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.25:
        s = _mix_reserved(rng)
    elif mode < 0.55:
        s = _rand_identifier(rng, max_parts=3)
    elif mode < 0.8:
        s = _random_ascii(rng)
    else:
        # Combine two identifiers with namespace-like separator
        left = _rand_identifier(rng, max_parts=2)
        right = _rand_identifier(rng, max_parts=2)
        sep = rng.choice(_NS_SEPARATORS)
        s = f"{left}{sep}{right}"
    s = _maybe_namespace(rng, s)
    # Clamp length (many stubs trim to <=32/64 chars); keep within 1..64
    if len(s) > 64:
        s = s[:64]
    if not s:
        s = "_id"
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Generate between 1 and 4 identifiers concatenated with newline, as FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # may be called multiple times for different roles. Newlines allow the fuzzer
    # harness to slice distinct strings out of the same buffer if needed.
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    items = []
    for _ in range(count):
        items.append(_build_identifier(rng))
    payload = "\n".join(items)
    # Ensure non-empty, ASCII, and <= 4096 bytes
    b = payload.encode('utf-8')
    if not b:
        b = b"_id"
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b
